section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: In natural first-language acquisition, the four language skills — Listening, Speaking, Reading, Writing (LSRW) — typically develop in which order?

options.option_text: All four develop simultaneously with no order

explanation: A child first listens and absorbs language, then speaks; reading and writing are literacy skills learned later, typically in school.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: A teacher explains new English words using objects, actions and pictures in the classroom, avoiding the mother tongue entirely. This is the:
explanation: The Direct Method teaches entirely through the target language itself — using realia, gestures and context rather than translation.

section: Language II English · Ch33 — Methodology of Teaching English
subject: Language II — English
stem: A teacher has pupils role-play ordering food at a restaurant, focusing on getting the message across rather than perfect grammar. This reflects:

options.option_text: Silent reading with no speaking practice

explanation: CLT prioritises real-life communicative competence and meaningful language use over strict grammatical accuracy.
